# designless-kotlin

> Your brand in a Kotlin or Android app. Colours, type, spacing and marks come from your published brand, and change when you publish.

designless-kotlin is the Kotlin and Android client for [Designless](https://designless.io), expression infrastructure for coding agents. It ships in two artifacts: `io.designless:serve`, a pure Kotlin/JVM protocol client with zero dependencies and no Android framework, and `io.designless:serve-android`, the Android layer covering typeface registration, colour and length conversion, a snapshot store, and foreground activation.

## About Designless

Designless is expression infrastructure: a runtime layer that gives coding agents access to encoded human design judgment, so the software they build carries taste and not just logic.

Design systems ship a file of tokens. You export it, paste it into a codebase, and hope it stays in sync. Expression infrastructure serves design decisions at runtime instead, to the agent, at the moment it builds. Designless calls the gap between what you express and what actually gets built the Expression Gap, and closes it by making the brand available as infrastructure rather than as a document.

This package is the delivery end of that: whatever an agent resolved and published as a brand, this is how a Kotlin or Android app reads it at runtime.

## What this package does

- Reads your published brand at runtime: colour, typography, spacing, and the rest of the token tree.
- Resolves brand marks to the addresses they are served at, at a closed ladder of sizes.
- Stages and registers brand typefaces, and reports honestly which of six outcomes a font request actually got, instead of silently substituting the platform font.
- Holds a fetched brand change until you activate it, so a brand never restyles a screen underneath someone mid-task.
- Converts published values into the units Android reads, including `#rrggbbaa` colours, which the platform's own parser will not accept.

## What this package does not do

- It carries no brand values of its own, so a brand change never requires a release of this package.
- It pulls in no JSON library and no serialization runtime. Dependency conflicts are the loudest complaint about Android libraries, and a thin client that drags in a serialization runtime is not thin.
- It ships no Compose theme, deliberately. A theme here would pin a Compose version on every consumer; the conversions that are easy to get wrong are provided instead.
- It picks no concurrency framework. An SDK that picks one picks it for the whole app.

## Install

```kotlin
dependencies {
    implementation("io.designless:serve-android:0.1.0")   // Android
    // or, on a plain JVM:
    implementation("io.designless:serve:0.1.0")
}
```

## Key concepts

- **Expression Infrastructure**: the runtime layer that makes design judgment available to agents as a service. Not a design tool and not a component library.
- **Brand Capsule**: a self-contained, versioned, deterministic compilation of everything defining how a brand looks, feels and speaks. This package consumes what a capsule publishes.
- **Expression Contracts**: design tokens name values; expression contracts encode intent, context and relationships. Tokens are a vocabulary list, contracts are a fluent speaker.
- **Taste as Infrastructure**: the thesis that design judgment can be encoded, structured and served the same way logic and data are.

## Sibling packages

The same brand, on other platforms:

- [designless-swift](https://github.com/designlesshq/designless-swift): iOS, macOS, tvOS, watchOS, visionOS
- [designless-dart](https://github.com/designlesshq/designless-dart): Dart and Flutter
- [designless-npm](https://github.com/designlesshq/designless-npm): web and React Native
